title: Workmanship Warranties General Condition: Number of Coverages a Customer Holds
content:
**Condition.** Under the Workmanship Warranties, a customer may hold any number of coverages, one for each piece of delivered or completed network work on any of their vehicles. Coverages on the same vehicle stand side by side, each covering only its own source work. Per source work, the limit on the coverages one source job may carry applies.

There is no maximum number of coverages per customer.

## What the condition means in practice

| Situation | Effect under the condition |
|---|---|
| A customer has had network work done on two different vehicles | Each piece of work carries its own coverage; the customer holds both. |
| One vehicle has had a glass replacement and, later, a collision repair | Two coverages stand side by side on that vehicle, the glass coverage covering only the glass work and the collision coverage covering only the collision repair. |
| A customer already holds several coverages | No maximum per customer applies; a further piece of delivered or completed network work carries its own coverage. |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A customer's vehicle carries a Glass Installation Lifetime Warranty from a windshield replacement and a Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty from a later repair. The glass coverage covers only the windshield installation, and the collision coverage covers only the collision repair; neither extends to the other's source work.
